title: Your Buyers Already Googled Your Last Building. Show It First

body:
Developers spend a fortune on the sales gallery and the renderings. Meanwhile, the buyer has already done their homework somewhere else, on a phone, before they ever walked in the door.

## What buyers check before they visit

Before a buyer steps into your sales gallery, they have already opened Google Maps. They have looked up your last building. Not the rendering of it, the real one. They have seen:

- The street view of the finished building
- The reviews people left about it
- The photos residents posted of the lobby on social media

This research happens whether you like it or not. The only choice you have is whether you are part of that conversation.

## Why hiding your last project backfires

If your last project is missing from your website and your presentation, buyers notice. They do not think you forgot. They think something is wrong with it. Silence about your past feels like a warning sign, even when the building is perfectly fine. The buyer still finds the street view and the reviews. The only difference is that now they find them without your context, and they wonder why you did not mention it.

## Show it first

When you put your last building up front, you answer the question the buyer was too polite to ask: did this developer deliver what they promised last time? You remove the doubt before it grows.

In my view, your last building is your best rendering, because it is the only one that is real. Every image of the new tower is a promise. The finished tower is proof.

## How to use your last building in your sales process

1. **Put it on the first page.** Make your completed project the first thing buyers see on your website and in your presentation.
2. **Take buyers there.** Invite serious buyers to visit the finished building in person.
3. **Let them talk to residents.** The people who live there are more convincing than any sales script.

This is how a promise becomes proof. A buyer who has walked through your last building and heard from the people inside it has far fewer reasons to doubt your next one.
takeaways: Buyers look up a developer's last building on Google Maps before visiting a sales gallery.
They see the real street view, the reviews and resident photos, not your renderings.
Hiding a past project makes buyers assume something is wrong.
Your last finished building is your best rendering because it is the only one that is real.
Put it on the first page, take buyers there and let them talk to residents.
faq: How do I check a real estate developer's track record?
Look up their completed buildings on Google Maps, read the reviews, check resident photos and, if possible, visit a finished project and talk to the people who live there.
Should developers show their past projects to presale buyers?
Yes. Showing a finished project first answers the biggest doubt buyers have and turns your promises into visible proof.
Why do buyers distrust new developments?
They are buying something that does not exist yet. Seeing what a developer delivered before is one of the strongest ways to reduce that doubt.
